title: Motion Observation Artifact (M2a)
description: What a page was seen to DO, and — separately — what caused it. Written by the motion-observation pass, which is independent of the forensic capture: it runs unfrozen, records timestamps, and is compared by classification rather than by bytes. Its contract version is separate so a change here can never invalidate a forensic capture.

$motionContract.description: Independent of CAPTURE_CONTRACT_VERSION. The two version different things.

apparatusRemaining.description: Elements still carrying an apparatus marker after cleanup. Asserted rather than assumed; anything but 0 means the page was left instrumented.

controls.description: Observations taken with no action, over comparable elapsed time. Without one, no causal claim can be licensed.

cleanup.description: What cleanup achieved, not what it attempted. Every key is present and starts null: a step that never ran and a step that ran and failed must be distinguishable.

reducedMotionRestored.description: Null when reduced motion was never changed. Reporting `true` for something untouched would claim a restoration that never happened.

claimType.description: `runtime-observation` says a state changed. It does NOT say why. A causal statement lives only in triggerClassification.

monotonicMs.description: From a monotonic clock, so elapsed time survives a wall-clock adjustment.

motionEvidenceClass.description: The motion-specific evidence axis, separate from the five-value STATUS vocabulary, which is unchanged.

controlObservationId.description: The control that licensed any causal claim on this record. Null means no causal claim can be made from it.

triggerClassification.description: Null on a control record — a control that classified its own trigger would be evidence for itself.
A causal claim, or an explicit refusal to make one. `verified` requires a control that saw no change over comparable elapsed time.

reason.description: Required in substance whenever the classification is `unverified`: a refusal with no stated reason is indistinguishable from an oversight.
